entry.title: SubcellPert: Benchmarking Subcellular Perturbation Prediction
entry.summary:
Perturbations change both RNA abundance and intracellular organization, but gene-count predictors omit the positions needed to model spatial responses. To address this limitation, we introduce textbf{textit{SubcellPert}}, a benchmark for perturbation-response prediction at single-RNA-molecule resolution. It comprises 14 imaging datasets with 13.88 million cells and 3.65 billion RNA molecules.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: LigRNA: High-accuracy prediction of RNA-ligand binding sites via dynamic chemical complementarity and language model encoding
entry.summary:
RNA-binding small molecules represent a validated therapeutic modality, yet pinpointing their exact RNA binding sites remains critical for mechanistic understanding and drug optimization. Experimental methods, while precise, are costly and low-throughput, necessitating robust computational alternatives. Approaches based on static feature concatenation may overlook input-dependent relationships between RNA residues and ligand functional groups.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #combinatorics #neuroscience

entry.title: HDOCK-Multimer: improved structure prediction of large protein complexes by integrating docking and combinatorial assembly
entry.summary:

entry.title: LLMs predict material properties based on atom types and not atom positions
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01044-3 Accurately predicting properties of materials is one of the main challenges in computational materials science. Systematic experiments now show that large language models (LLMs) struggle to use positional information for the prediction of those properties. This limitation does not reverse as model or dataset sizes grow.

Source: Nature Computational Science · Tags: #bioinformatics #materials-science

entry.title: HIP: Hessian Interatomic Potentials without derivatives
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01066-x The authors introduce an extension of machine learning interatomic potentials that predicts molecular Hessians directly, improving accuracy and speed compared in transition-state searches, geometry optimization and vibrational analysis relative to Hessians from automatic differentiation.

Source: Nature Computational Science · Tags: #bioinformatics #materials-science

entry.title: Less can be more for predicting properties with large language models
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01045-2 Researchers show that large language models cannot learn from spatial coordinates regardless of model or data scale. Specialized geometric neural networks consistently outperform language models for material property prediction.

Source: Nature Computational Science · Tags: #bioinformatics #materials-science #neuroscience

entry.title: Epidemiological modeling in the age of artificial intelligence
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 09 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01070-1 Artificial intelligence is enabling epidemic models to learn across outbreaks. The next challenge is ensuring that these models learn and transfer not mere statistical patterns, but epidemiological mechanisms.
